items.title: Show HN: TempCD – Temporarily CD in a directory with one command
items.contentSnippet:
TempCD is just a small thing I made, its only purpose it to eliminate having to enter cd again after only wanting to do one command in a directory. Super simple, just:
> tcd ~/example
~/example> command
command output
>
That's it, just returns you back to where you were before without having to type cd again.

items.title: Show HN: KittyBrowser, I built a web browser in your terminal
items.contentSnippet:
I'm spending more time in the terminal, and with kitty graphics support now in Ghostty and Rex, I thought a real browser in a coding pane might be possible. It is.
kb drives headless Chrome and draws each frame as pixels, so you get the actual page, not a text approximation.
Key features:
- Built in Rust, on headless Chrome
- Keyboard shortcuts, mouse clicks, scroll, zoom, find, copy
- Frames can go through the terminal itself, so it should work over SSH

items.title: Show HN: A shared live Etch A Sketch – one continuous line, or draw via API
items.contentSnippet:
I made a live Etch A Sketch that everyone draws on together. It's one shared 4000×4000 canvas, and you see other people's pens moving in real time. Like the real toy, you only get one continuous line and can only draw or erase.
If you want to draw something more intricate, there's a free API you can post your stroke coordinates strokes to: https://graciegould.com/api/etch/stroke (example under the API button on the page).

items.title: Show HN: Autoresearch, but for Weight Space Programming
items.contentSnippet:
I built Vespasian to let everyone experiment with weight space editing. Pick task, provide data, add API key and it takes care of the rest. In addition to the Rust crate, it now runs interactively and without an install on HF Spaces. There’s never been a better time to try out weight space programming. Throw your tasks at it and see how far you can get without gradients.
